items.phonicsTarget: First alphabet sounds: m, s, t, p
items.japaneseHint: 文字の名前ではなく、単語の最初に聞こえる短い音を意識します。mは唇を閉じ、sは息を細く出します。
items.mouthTip: Close both lips for /m/. For /s/, keep a narrow air channel. Release /t/ and /p/ without adding a vowel.
items.practiceSentence: Sam taps the map.
items.audioFocus: Listen for the first sounds in moon, sun, top, and pen.

items.phonicsTarget: Alphabet sounds: n, b, d, g
items.japaneseHint: nは舌先、bは両唇、dは上の歯ぐき、gは喉の奥を使います。後ろに「ウ」を足さないようにします。
items.mouthTip: Touch the ridge behind your upper teeth for /n/ and /d/. Close the lips for /b/ and use the back of the tongue for /g/.
items.practiceSentence: Ben digs by the big bed.
items.audioFocus: Listen for the first sounds in net, bag, dog, and gum.

items.phonicsTarget: Breathy and voiced consonants: f, v, h, w
items.japaneseHint: fとvは上の歯を下唇に軽く当てます。vでは喉を震わせます。hは息、wは丸い唇から始めます。
items.mouthTip: Let air pass between the upper teeth and lower lip for /f/ and /v/. Voice only /v/. Round the lips before /w/.
items.practiceSentence: We have five hats.
items.audioFocus: Listen to fan and van. Feel your voice start in van.

items.phonicsTarget: L and r, plus c, k, j, z, y, x, and q
items.japaneseHint: lは舌先を上の歯ぐきにつけ、rでは舌を後ろへ引いて上につけません。cはcatでは/k/、xはboxでは/ks/、qはquizでは/kw/です。
items.mouthTip: For /l/, touch the ridge behind the upper teeth with the tongue tip. For /r/, raise or bunch the tongue without touching the roof. Use the back of the tongue for /k/ and keep final /ks/ together.
items.practiceSentence: Look right at the red fox.
items.audioFocus: Listen to light and right. Then try the other first and last sounds.

items.japaneseHint: 日本語の「ア」より口を横にも開き、明るく短く発音します。
items.mouthTip: Lower the jaw, spread the lips slightly, and keep the tongue low and forward.
items.practiceSentence: A black cat sat on the mat.
items.audioFocus: Listen to the short vowel in cat.

items.japaneseHint: 「イー」と伸ばさず、力を抜いた短い「イ」にします。
items.mouthTip: Keep the jaw relaxed and the tongue high but loose. End quickly without smiling too widely.
items.practiceSentence: Six fish swim in the river.
items.audioFocus: Listen to the short vowel in sit.

items.japaneseHint: UKでは唇を少し丸めた短い音、USでは口を大きく開く音になりやすいです。
items.mouthTip: Drop the jaw and keep the sound short. Use slightly rounder lips for the common UK pronunciation.
items.practiceSentence: Tom drops the box by the clock.
items.audioFocus: Listen to the vowel in hot. Notice how each accent sounds.

items.japaneseHint: 「イ」にならないよう、口を少し開けて短い「エ」にします。
items.mouthTip: Keep the tongue at mid height and the lips relaxed. Do not glide toward /iː/.
items.practiceSentence: Meg left her red pen on the desk.
items.audioFocus: Listen to the short vowel in bed.

items.japaneseHint: 口を丸めず、のどの中央から短く「ア」に近い音を出します。
items.mouthTip: Relax the lips and jaw. Keep the tongue central and avoid rounding as for /uː/.
items.practiceSentence: The duck runs under the bus.
items.audioFocus: Listen to the short vowel in sun.

items.phonicsTarget: CVC blending and clear final consonants
items.japaneseHint: 3つの音を切り離さずにつなぎ、最後の子音の後に母音を足さない練習です。
items.mouthTip: Join the first consonant to the vowel, then finish with the last consonant. Do not add a vowel after it.
items.practiceSentence: Kim can hop and run.
items.audioFocus: Join the sounds into a word. Listen for the final consonant.

items.japaneseHint: 最初の2子音の間に「ウ」や「オ」を入れず、一息でつなぎます。
items.mouthTip: Make the first consonant briefly, then move the tongue tip directly to /l/ without releasing a vowel.
items.practiceSentence: The blue flag flies above the plane.
items.audioFocus: Listen to both consonants at the start of blue.

items.japaneseHint: 子音の直後に英語のrへ移動します。間に日本語の母音を入れません。
items.mouthTip: Keep the tongue tip away from the roof of the mouth for /r/ and move into the following vowel smoothly.
items.practiceSentence: A green frog rests by the tree.
items.audioFocus: Listen to both consonants at the start of brown.

items.japaneseHint: sの後に母音を入れず、次の子音へすぐ移ります。streetは3子音を一続きにします。
items.mouthTip: Hold a thin /s/ airflow, shape the next consonant immediately, and release into the vowel only once.
items.practiceSentence: The strong swimmer starts slowly.
items.audioFocus: Keep the first consonants together. Listen to spin and street.

items.japaneseHint: shは息だけの「シュ」、chは最初に舌で空気を止めてから出す「チュ」に近い音です。
items.mouthTip: Round the lips slightly for both. For /tʃ/, briefly block the air before releasing it; for /ʃ/, let air flow continuously.
items.practiceSentence: She chose fresh fish for lunch.
items.audioFocus: Listen to ship and chip. The start of chip has a short stop.

items.japaneseHint: 舌先を歯の間に軽く出します。thinkは息だけ、thisは喉を震わせます。
items.mouthTip: Place the tongue tip gently between the teeth. Blow air for /θ/ and add voice for /ð/ without pulling the tongue back.
items.practiceSentence: Those three things are over there.
items.audioFocus: Listen to think and this. Your voice starts in this.

items.japaneseHint: whは多くの話者でw、phはf、ngは舌先を上につけず鼻へ抜く1つの音です。
items.mouthTip: Round the lips for /w/. Touch upper teeth to lower lip for /f/. For /ŋ/, lift the back of the tongue and keep the tip down.
items.practiceSentence: When will Phil sing that long song?
items.audioFocus: Listen to when, phone, and sing. Keep the end of sing smooth.

items.japaneseHint: 最後のeは読まず、その前のaを文字名の/eɪ/に変えます。 ここでの語に共通するパターンです。have・give・loveのような例外もあります。
items.mouthTip: Begin with a mid-front vowel and glide upward. Keep the final consonant clear; do not pronounce the final e.
items.practiceSentence: Jake made a cake by the lake.
items.audioFocus: Listen to cap, then cape. The vowel changes.

items.japaneseHint: 最後のeは無音で、iは/aɪ/になります。短いiのsitと比べます。 ここでの語に共通するパターンです。have・give・loveのような例外もあります。
items.mouthTip: Start with an open vowel and glide toward /ɪ/. Stop on the final consonant without sounding the e.
items.practiceSentence: Mike rides his bike at five.
items.audioFocus: Listen to bit, then bite. The vowel changes.

items.japaneseHint: 最後のeは読まず、oを滑らかな/oʊ/にします。hopとhopeを聞き分けます。 ここでの語に共通するパターンです。have・give・loveのような例外もあります。
items.mouthTip: Begin with relaxed lips, then round them as the vowel glides. Keep the last consonant distinct.
items.practiceSentence: Rose wrote a note at home.
items.audioFocus: Listen to hop, then hope. The vowel changes.

items.phonicsTarget: Silent e patterns with u and e
items.japaneseHint: u_eは/juː/または/uː/、e_eは/iː/になります。最後のeは発音しません。 ここでの語に共通するパターンです。have・give・loveのような例外もあります。
items.mouthTip: For /juː/, begin with a light y sound before rounded /uː/. For /iː/, keep the tongue high and smile slightly.
items.practiceSentence: June chose these cute cubes.
items.audioFocus: Listen to cub and cube. Then listen to these.

items.phonicsTarget: Long a vowel teams ai and ay
items.japaneseHint: aiは語の中、ayは語末に多く、どちらも/eɪ/を表すことが多いです。
items.mouthTip: Start at a clear mid vowel and glide upward. Keep it one syllable rather than separating e and i.
items.practiceSentence: We may take the train on a rainy day.
items.audioFocus: Listen to the same vowel in rain and day.

items.phonicsTarget: Long e vowel teams ee and ea
items.japaneseHint: eeとeaは長い/iː/になることが多いですが、headやbreadのeaは短い/e/です。
items.mouthTip: Keep the tongue high and front with lightly spread lips. Hold the sound without adding a second vowel.
items.practiceSentence: The team reads beneath the green tree.
items.audioFocus: Listen to the long vowel in green and leaf.

items.phonicsTarget: Long o vowel teams oa and ow
items.japaneseHint: oaは語の中、owは語末に多く、滑らかな/oʊ/になります。ただしcowのowは/aʊ/です。
items.mouthTip: Glide from a neutral rounded vowel to tighter lips. Do not split the vowel team into two syllables.
items.practiceSentence: The boat moves slowly past the yellow house.
items.audioFocus: Listen to the same vowel in boat and snow.

items.japaneseHint: moonのooは長い/uː/、bookのooは短い/ʊ/です。つづりだけでは判断できない語もあります。
items.mouthTip: Round the lips for both. Hold /uː/ longer with a tenser tongue; keep /ʊ/ short and relaxed.
items.practiceSentence: The cook put good food by the cool pool.
items.audioFocus: Listen to fool and full. Compare the two vowels.

items.japaneseHint: US英語では母音からrへ滑らかにつなぎます。UK英語では後ろに母音がなければrを発音しないことがあります。
items.mouthTip: For US /r/, pull the tongue slightly back without touching the roof. Avoid adding a Japanese vowel after r.
items.practiceSentence: A short storm passed over the farm.
items.audioFocus: Listen to car and core. Notice how each accent treats the ending.

items.phonicsTarget: R-controlled spellings er, ir, and ur
items.japaneseHint: er・ir・urは多くの語で似た音になります。USではrを響かせ、UKでは長い中央母音になります。
items.mouthTip: Keep the lips relaxed. In US English, curl or bunch the tongue without touching the roof; in UK English, sustain the central vowel.
items.practiceSentence: The first bird returned on Thursday.
items.audioFocus: Listen to the vowel in her, bird, and turn.

items.japaneseHint: 唇を丸めた音から短い「イ」へ、1音節の中で滑らかに移動します。
items.mouthTip: Begin with rounded lips, then relax and raise the tongue toward /ɪ/. Do not make two separate beats.
items.practiceSentence: The boy enjoyed choosing a shiny coin.
items.audioFocus: Listen to the moving vowel in coin and boy.

items.japaneseHint: 大きく開いた音から唇を丸める方向へ移動します。snowのowは/oʊ/なので注意します。
items.mouthTip: Drop the jaw for the first part, then lift it while rounding the lips. Keep the glide within one syllable.
items.practiceSentence: A brown cow walked around the town.
items.audioFocus: Listen to the moving vowel in house and cow.

items.phonicsTarget: Common spelling choices: c, k, ck, soft c, soft g, and dge
items.japaneseHint: cはe・i・yの前で/s/になりやすく、gも同じ位置で/dʒ/になることがあります。短母音の後の/k/はckが多いです。
items.mouthTip: Use the back of the tongue for /k/ and /g/. For /dʒ/, briefly stop the air, then release it with voice.
items.practiceSentence: The giant placed a badge beside the city clock.
items.audioFocus: Listen to the sounds in cat, city, giant, and bridge.

items.japaneseHint: 語尾はつづりではなく直前の音で変わります。余分な音節を足すのは/ɪz/と/ɪd/の場合だけです。
items.mouthTip: Keep voicing on for /z/ and /d/ endings. Add a full extra syllable only after sibilants for -es or after /t, d/ for -ed.
items.practiceSentence: She washed the cups, cleaned the trays, and packed the boxes.
items.audioFocus: Listen to the endings. Some add a beat, and some do not.

items.phonicsTarget: Word stress, schwa, and r-colored weak vowels
items.sound: /ə/ in unstressed syllables; /ɚ/ in some unstressed US endings
items.japaneseHint: 強勢のない母音は、はっきりしたア・イ・ウではなく、短く弱い/ə/になることがあります。US英語のteacherなどの語末では、rを伴う/ɚ/になることもあります。
items.mouthTip: Relax the jaw and tongue for schwa. Make the stressed syllable longer, clearer, and slightly louder. In US English, keep a light r-color in endings such as “teacher”; UK English commonly uses a non-rhotic weak vowel there.
items.practiceSentence: A computer can support a family project.
items.audioFocus: Listen for the strong beat. Keep the other syllables light.

items.phonicsTarget: Sentence rhythm, linking, and reduced function words
items.sound: stressed content words with linked, reduced grammar words
items.japaneseHint: 大切な内容語を強くし、短い機能語は弱くします。単語末の子音を次の母音へつなぐと自然なリズムになります。
items.mouthTip: Tap a steady beat on key words. Let final consonants connect to following vowels, and reduce “to,” “a,” and “of” instead of stressing every word.
items.practiceSentence: Could you send it over when you arrive?
items.audioFocus: Listen for the main beats. Connect the words smoothly.
